onedevR

onedevr is an R client for the OneDev REST API — issues, projects, builds, and pull requests, for OneDev.

Note: This code was written with AI assistance and is not yet thoroughly tested. Review results carefully before relying on them, and please report problems in the issue tracker.

References:

  • R package shape (GitLab → R): gitlabr — low-level od_request() escape hatch + high-level od_* wrappers, same idea as gitlab / gl_*.
  • Working with OneDev itself: tod (TheOneDev CLI) — issue/PR/build refs, query DSL, and API conventions to mirror when implementing / extending onedevr.

Motivation

onedevr was born from a practical constraint: restricted development environments.

Many corporate environments restrict tooling to essential languages only. If your development environment is confined to R and Git, you cannot use the official tod CLI (e.g., due to firewall restrictions or tooling policies). Yet you still need to interact with OneDev for:

  • Running builds, managing artifacts, querying repositories
  • Automating issue/PR workflows within R scripts or Quarto documents
  • Leveraging AI-assisted coding workflows that need programmatic OneDev access

onedevr solves this by: 1. Removing the tod dependency — communicate directly with OneDev’s REST API from R 2. Enabling AI-assisted workflows — your coding AI (Claude, etc.) can use onedevr to interact with OneDev on your behalf 3. Being AI-efficient — clean, predictable function naming (od_*), consistent parameter patterns, and comprehensive documentation so LLMs can reason about the API without ambiguity

If your constraint is “I have R, I have Git, I need OneDev”, onedevr is for you.

Status

v0.7.1 — current release. Issue/build/PR workflows, boards, jobs, packages, repository helpers, tibbles by default, and Bearer + Basic Auth. 0.7.0 added iteration names wherever iteration ids are accepted, credential-safe caching, query-string escaping, masked secrets when printing a connection, and automated security and vulnerability monitoring (see SECURITY.md). 0.7.1 adds od_whoami() (current user, with a fallback when /users/me is refused), automatic paging for count above 100, shorter error messages for HTML error pages, and a diagnosis script for the HTTP 500 on issue comments. See NEWS.md for the full changelog.

remotes::install_github("alexseymer/onedevR")

Documentation: (also available on pkgdown site) - Getting started — Installation, config, basic workflows - Issues workflow — Querying, creating, updating, automation - Builds workflow — Build management, artifacts, CI/CD - Pull requests workflow — PR review, commenting, merging - Contributing — Development setup, testing, documentation standards

Quick start 

library(onedevr)

# Env-based (fine for interactive use)
Sys.setenv(
  ONEDEV_HOST = "https://git.example.test",
  ONEDEV_API_TOKEN = "your-token",
  ONEDEV_PROJECT_PATH = "group/my-project"
)

od_query_issues(state = "Open")
issue <- od_get_issue(145)
fields <- od_get_issue_fields(145)

# Or an explicit connection (preferred in scripts)
conn <- od_connection(
  host = "https://git.example.test",
  token = Sys.getenv("ONEDEV_API_TOKEN"),
  project_path = "group/my-project"
)

iterations <- od_list_iterations(conn = conn)
created <- od_create_issue(
  title = "API test",
  description = "Created from R",
  fields = list(Priority = "Normal"),
  iteration_ids = iterations$id[1],  # ids or names, e.g. "Version 3.0.0"
  conn = conn
)

od_issue_set_title(created$number, "API test (renamed)", conn = conn)
od_issue_transition_state(created$number, "Closed", conn = conn)

# Builds & pull requests
builds <- od_query_builds(status = "successful", count = 10L, conn = conn)
pr <- od_get_pull_request(1, conn = conn)
comments <- od_get_pull_request_comments(1, conn = conn)

# Projects & users
projects <- od_query_projects(count = 20L, conn = conn)
me <- od_get_me(conn = conn)

Copy .Renviron.example to .Renviron (gitignored) and fill in your host/token/project. .env.example is the same variable list for non-R tooling. Live integration tests are gated behind ONEDEV_RUN_LIVE_TESTS=1.

Scope and maturity

onedevr aims to be a general-purpose R client for the OneDev REST API. Functions differ in how well they are proven:

  • Core (issues, comments, iterations, boards, pull requests, projects, connection): used in daily work against a real instance; bugs found there are fixed and covered by regression tests.
  • Experimental (batch, parallel, streaming, caching, webhooks, SSH keys): tested offline only, marked “Experimental” on their help pages; the interface may change.
  • Everything else (builds, jobs, packages, repository, users, groups) is tested offline and partly read-verified.

Live verification of the whole surface is the next milestone (see ROADMAP.md).

What’s in v0.7.x

  • Issues, boards, builds, PRs, jobs, packages, and repository (branches/tags/commits/files)
  • Board helpers: od_list_boards(), od_get_board(), od_query_board_issues()
  • Iterations by name or id: od_get_iteration(), od_resolve_iteration_ids()
  • Status keywords for builds/PRs, query DSL helpers, and od_paginate()
  • Tibbles by default for list queries; od_connection() or env-based config
  • Bearer token or Basic Auth; od_request() escape hatch for custom endpoints
  • Security: secrets are masked when printed, credentials are only sent to the configured host, and dependencies are audited against OSV in CI
  • Workflow vignettes (issues, builds, PRs) plus getting-started and function map

Security

Tokens and passwords are masked when a connection is printed, credentials are only sent to the configured host, and the dependencies are audited against the OSV database in CI. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

Design notes worth knowing up front

  • Issue / build / PR numbers are UI numbers, not internal IDs. OneDev #145 (what you see in the UI) is a different value from the internal REST id. The high-level API always takes the UI number; see §9 of the plan / tod ref formats. Resolution tries projectPath#n, then bare #n / n for OneDev versions that reject path-prefixed numbers.
  • Some OneDev endpoints accept more than one payload shape depending on version/installation (e.g. issue creation, state transitions, iterations). onedevr tries known variants rather than picking one and failing silently on others — see §10 of the plan.
  • Query errors: "Title" contains "…" is often rejected with HTTP 406 “Invalid query”. Use fuzzy text ~text~ and board-exact state names; check od_get_query_description("issue"). Failing request-body variants are reported together, so the real cause is not hidden.
  • Custom issue fields are installation-specific. There’s no fixed schema; fields is treated as a named list.
  • Connections: pass conn = od_connection(...) per call, or od_set_connection(conn) for a package default. Env vars remain the fallback. Bearer token is default; Basic Auth via username/password (or ONEDEV_USERNAME / ONEDEV_PASSWORD).
  • List queries return tibbles by default (od_query_issues(), etc.). Use as_tibble = FALSE or options(onedevr.as_tibble = FALSE) for raw lists. Single-object getters stay as lists.
